comparator.name: Bachelor in Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted ESSB EER 2026–2027 Appendix III A p.37 defines this whole Dutch-language 180-EC Sociology curriculum: 60 EC per year, required 15-EC internship, 15-EC research project and 15-EC bachelor project, plus an open 15-EC minor. No specialised route or minor subject is imposed. Designing Social Research uses the correctly spelled current official study-page title; the EER table contains a typographical error.

alternatives.label: Sociology & social research
alternatives.concept: Sociological theory and qualitative and quantitative research anchor a programme in social change. Politics, economics, history and social psychology provide complementary ways to study institutions, inequality and collective life.
alternatives.labelReason: The full UCR sociology sequence and social research methods anchor a wider combination of social-science and historical perspectives. The title does not claim a dedicated demographic or urban-sociology sequence.
progression: Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology and then Contemporary Social Theory. Basic research methods precede multivariate statistics. Introductory politics precedes advanced EU and conflict study. PPD is completed in the first year.

alternatives.label: Politics, inequality & social change
alternatives.concept: Sociology, law, politics and history examine how institutions shape rights, inequality and social change. Empirical methods and public economics support policy analysis, while gender and Indigenous histories examine specific experiences of exclusion.
alternatives.labelReason: The label reflects the completed sociology, politics, law, public-economics and history mix.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the primary programme, constitutional and EU law, human rights, Indigenous histories and workplace diversity replace its public-health, behavioural-economic, quantitative and environmental contributions. The alternative studies inequality through rights and political institutions, rather than merely relabelling the same sociology courses.
progression: Introduction to Sociology now precedes Modern Sociology, which precedes Contemporary Social Theory. The law gateway precedes constitutional and EU law. Research foundations precede public economics and applied diversity management.

alternatives.label: Society, sustainability & technology
alternatives.concept: Social theory and empirical methods examine how technology and environmental change affect work, institutions and public decisions. Climate and life-cycle analysis supply environmental evidence, while organisational psychology and AI-related study address changes in work and organisations.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme studies society, sustainability and technological change; its technical courses are supporting methods or environmental evidence, not a substitute for sociological inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: Environmental assessment, climate/governance, sustainability research, organisational psychology, AI and data/programming methods implement a specific societal-transitions inquiry. Generic AI planning/optimisation and waves/materials instruction have been removed; the difference from the primary and rights/politics alternatives follows the concept rather than threshold-filling substitutions.
progression: Sociology progresses across three separate autumn terms. Research methods precede multivariate statistics and organisational psychology; ethical reasoning precedes AI Ethics. Climate and sustainability foundations precede life-cycle analysis and the applied sustainability research project. Programming supplies computational methods without inventing a technology-specific social dataset.

candidates.label: Planetary sociology, sustainability and technological change

selection.assessment: Three substantive, coherent and feasible programmes are retained. A separate population/family/cities/migration candidate is explicitly recorded rather than falsely claimed as fully implemented by the closest programme; no fourth programme is added beyond the maximum.

blocks: Both courses introduce sociology's central concepts, classical theories and methods for analysing social relations and institutions; the UCR course is a direct disciplinary counterpart.

Modern Sociology engages major sociological theories and debates about modernity, providing a direct counterpart to the comparator's study of foundational sociological texts, though it organises the material as a modern-theory course rather than a key-texts survey.
Qualitative Research Methodology directly covers research design, qualitative data collection, interpretation, dissemination and researcher positionality in the study of social processes.

Statistics & Experimental Methods directly develops multivariate statistical analysis, model selection, execution and reporting for research in sociology and adjacent fields. Its experimental and behavioural-science framing is narrower than a full sociology-specific quantitative-methods sequence.

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory directly studies advanced global debates in sociological theory, including civil society, solidarity, social trust and decolonial critique. Its thematic focus is narrower than the comparator's general theoretical-sociology component.

Social Movements & Environmental Justice examines structural inequality, exclusion and collective responses through environmental-justice cases. It therefore covers a substantial applied part of the broader social-inequality component rather than its full sociological scope.

Foundations of Comparative Politics directly introduces political institutions, regimes and comparative empirical analysis. It covers a central political-science domain while placing more emphasis on comparative politics than a general political-science survey.

Histories of Gender examines identities, marginalisation, gendered institutions and cultural representation through historical inquiry and interviews. It is a substantial historical case-based counterpart to culture and identity, with narrower thematic and geographical scope; generic social psychology was the weaker previous placement.

Peace & Conflict directly examines the causes and dynamics of conflict, structural inequality, identity-based grievances and peacebuilding. It covers the conflict side of the broader cohesion-and-conflict component, while giving less attention to social cohesion outside conflict settings.

Research Methods & Statistics directly teaches research design, operationalisation, sampling and empirical project planning. It also adds introductory statistics, so it is broader methodologically than the comparator's research-design component.

Public Economics directly analyses government intervention, taxation, public spending, redistribution and the effects of policy on efficiency and equity. It covers the economic-policy part of the broader Public Policy component rather than public policy as a whole.

Climate Change devotes substantial study to societal transformation, health, migration, climate justice and governance alongside physical science. This supplies a climate-focused partial counterpart to planetary sociology, not its full sociological scope.

Both components organise students to carry out a research project. UCR Research in a Sustainable Delta is a 7.5-EC team project with an external partner in sustainability, whereas the external 15-EC project is specifically sociological. The shared educational research function is partial and does not reproduce the credit volume or disciplinary scope.

Personal & Professional Development explicitly develops critical source analysis, academic writing, presentations, collaboration and reflection. It is a stronger broad academic-skills counterpart than the specialised persuasion course; the external 8-EC Skills component also contains discipline-specific research and policy skills.

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines organisational structure, culture, groups, power and management. This provides a stronger substantial organisational counterpart than the former entrepreneurship/startup course; its psychological emphasis differs from the broad external organisation-and-management course.

Introduction to Economics provides useful background on markets, firms and unemployment but does not directly study population change, family relations and work as a sociological and demographic field. No scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart.

The comparator component focuses specifically on urban sociology and migration. The scheduled UCR courses provide related political, historical and sociological context but no course directly combines cities and migration as its principal subject.
The comparator requires a 15-EC placement in professional sociological practice. No scheduled UCR course constitutes an internship or reproduces that sustained placement function.

The comparator reserves 15 EC as a formal minor or exchange block. UCR's open curriculum offers choice throughout the programme but no scheduled course represents an equivalent reserved profiling block.

Onderzoek in de Praktijk translates sociological research into professional practice and communication for a chosen field. Several UCR courses contain applied or community-engaged work, but none has this specific sociology-to-practice function.

The Bachelor Project is a 15-EC independently executed sociological study. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is an equivalent bachelor thesis or independent capstone, so the component remains unmatched.

notes.text: The Erasmus bachelor includes a structured sociological sequence, a required 15-EC internship and a required 15-EC bachelor project. The UCR programmes retain related academic inquiry but do not reproduce those requirements or the same specialist preparation.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines social change through theory, qualitative and quantitative research, and work with professional organisations. Its curriculum addresses inequality, population and family life, culture and identity, cities and migration, cohesion and conflict, and planetary change.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes combine sociological theory and research with other fields: broad social inquiry; politics, rights and inequality; or society, sustainability and technology. They offer meaningful related study, while the dedicated population/family and urban/migration sequence and the required 15-EC internship and 15-EC bachelor project remain gaps.

curriculum.limitation: The 180-EC programme includes a 15-EC internship, a 15-EC research project, a 15-EC bachelor project and an open 15-EC minor. No minor subject is assumed.

componentNotes.soc-culture: The UCR counterpart studies gender and identity through a particular historical context; it is narrower than the general sociological component.
componentNotes.soc-policy: The UCR counterpart addresses economic policy, rather than the full field of public policy.
componentNotes.soc-planet: The UCR counterpart combines climate-related social questions with substantial natural science.

cellNotes.text: This is a 7.5-EC sustainability research project with an external partner, rather than the 15-EC sociological research project.
